entities.title: The same game in every browser and on the server
entities.summary: The engine must give bit-identical results everywhere.
entities.requirement: Engine code uses only + − × ÷ and Math.sqrt (its own sine, cosine and arctangent from dmath.ts), and draws random numbers only from its own seeded generator, so a game replays exactly in every browser and in the Worker, and online browsers stay in step.
entities.measuredBy: The replay and lockstep tests: a recorded game replays to the same scores; the same seed and inputs replay the same game; dmath agrees with Math to 1e-12; browsers in lockstep play the same steps.

origin.description: The repository's agent instructions: the games' engines must stay deterministic.

entities.title: Replays are cheap for the server
entities.summary: The Worker replays a whole game, up to 90 minutes and nine players, on every submission, so a replay must be fast.
entities.requirement: Replaying a game takes under 200 ms per minute of play.
entities.measuredBy: test/replay.test.ts, "replaying a long game is quick enough for the server": a four-player co-op game.

sources.symbol: replaying a long game is quick enough for the server

entities.title: Everything from this origin
entities.summary: The page loads nothing from elsewhere except Cloudflare Web Analytics.
entities.requirement: The page's content security policy allows scripts, styles, images and connections only from icelander.net (WebSockets to wss://icelander.net included), plus Cloudflare's analytics beacon; no framing, forms, plugins or base URL changes. Camera, microphone, location and payment are refused; gamepads are allowed for this origin.
entities.measuredBy: public/_headers, read by Cloudflare's static assets; the scores page carries its own policy from worker/look.ts.

entities.title: The same speed on every screen
entities.summary: The game advances 60 steps a second whatever the display's refresh rate.
entities.requirement: The page steps the engine in fixed steps of 1/60 s from the time elapsed, catching up at most 0.25 s after a stall, so a game plays the same on a 60 Hz and a 144 Hz screen and its recording replays to the same game.
entities.measuredBy: Reading main.ts's frame loop; no automated check.
